translations.source_sense_description: transitiv ein Ergebnis durch Rechnen ermitteln

glosses: To calculate.

examples.text: Can you work out 250 × 12 in your head for me?
Can you work out how to get to the university by car?
You don't have to be Einstein to work out that this level of government subsidy is unsustainable.

glosses: To make sense of.

examples.text: I can't work these instructions out.

glosses: To decide.

examples.text: I can't work out if I like him or not.

glosses: To bring about or cause to happen by work or effort.

examples.text: Near-synonyms: hash out, hammer out
I think we can work out a compromise.
"Ah! if man would but see that hope is from within and not from without - that he himself must work out his own salvation!"

glosses: To resolve; to find a solution for.

examples.text: Near-synonyms: straighten out, sort out
They managed to work out their differences.
Trump hinted that Britain might be spared tariffs, saying: “I think that one can be worked out”.

glosses: To develop or devise in detail; to elaborate.

examples.text: Near-synonyms: plan out, lay out
to work out a plan

glosses: To smooth or perfect.

examples.text: Near-synonyms: iron out, smooth out
This is a beta version; we're still working out the kinks.

glosses: To conclude with the correct solution.

examples.text: Near-synonym: add up
These figures just don't work out.

glosses: To succeed; to result in a satisfactory situation.

examples.text: Near-synonym: pan out
Are you still seeing John? – No, it didn't work out.
As everyone knows, almost all booked passenger and freight trains are diagrammed into rosters for engines and men, and in an operating Utopia everything would work out daily according to plan.

glosses: To exercise, especially by lifting weights.

examples.text: John won't be here for a while because he's working out.
Wow, you're looking good! Do you work out?

glosses: To strengthen a part of one’s body by exercise.

examples.text: To work out your core
Hot, worked-out body and a creative mind possessed by this hunky, handsome, married guy.

glosses: To earn a wage working away from one's farm.

examples.text: The two Russians made good farmhands, and in summer they worked out together.
[…] with them good wages, maybe a fella can get hisself a little piece a land an’ work out for extra cash.

glosses: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see work, out.

examples.text: Using some tweezers, he worked the bee sting out of his hand.
He works out of a small office shared with three others.

glosses: To remove all the mineral that can be profitably exploited.

examples.text: The gravel pit had been worked out.
A worked-out chalk pit or quarry

translations.source_sense_description: transitiv ein Ergebnis durch Rechnen ermitteln

glosses: To determine the value of something or the solution to something by a mathematical process.

examples.text: Calculate the square root of 3 to 10 decimal places.

glosses: To determine values or solutions by a mathematical process; reckon.
To plan; to expect; to think.

examples.text: I stumbled along through the young pines and huckleberry bushes. Pretty soon I struck into a sort of path that, I cal’lated, might lead to the road I was hunting for. It twisted and turned, and, the first thing I knew, made a sudden bend around a bunch of bayberry scrub and opened out into a big clear space like a lawn.

glosses: To ascertain or predict by mathematical or astrological computations the time, circumstances, or other conditions of; to forecast or compute the character or consequences of.

examples.text: to calculate or cast one’s nativity
A cunning man did calculate my birth.

glosses: To adjust for purpose; to adapt by forethought or calculation; to fit or prepare by the adaptation of means to an end.

examples.text: to calculate a system of laws for the government and protection of a free people
[Religion] is […] calculated for our benefit.

glosses: To imagine sequences of potential moves and responses without actually moving the pieces.

translations.source_sense_description: transitiv ein Ergebnis durch Rechnen ermitteln

glosses: Déterminer un nombre au moyen d’un calcul ou de calculs.

examples.text: La taxe sera calculée en prenant cette charge complète comme unité, quels que soient le nombre et le cubage des wagons réellement employés pour le transport.
Parce que l’astronomie parvenait à calculer les tables de la lune, on a cru que le but de toute science était de prévoir avec exactitude l’avenir; […].
Nonante lieues en quatre étapes et une demie. Tu calcules ? Vingt lieues par jour ! Diâle, on routait dur en ce temps-là.
Après avoir calculé le temps nécessaire pour sortir de la cuisine et venir tirer le cordon placé sous la porte, il resonna encore de manière à produire un carillon très significatif.

— Sans remonter au Déluge, l’évaluation des récits bibliques à l’aune de la science ne date pas d’hier. Elle est même vieille comme Hérode. Mais l’« étoile » des Mages est sans doute l’évènement qui a le plus fait calculer les astronomes.

glosses: Combiner ou apprécier quelque chose.

examples.text: Prenait-on le rez-de-chaussée d’une tour, les étages supérieurs conservaient les moyens de reprendre l’offensive et d’écraser l’ennemi. On voit que tout était calculé pour une lutte possible pied à pied.
Calculer les chances de succès. Calculer les événements. Calculer ses démarches.

glosses: Considérer personnellement.

examples.text: — À voir ta face, je calcule que ce sont des nouvelles de malchance.

Tout homme que le Bon Dieu a créé sur la terre, tout homme a le droit d'avoir une douzième année …. … Après, se faire instruire, ça c'est une autre affaire. … Ça c'est prendre des cours, rentrer à l'université. Ça c'est autre chose, mais une douzième année, moi, je calcule que c'est logique. On a le droit d'avoir ça […].

glosses: Prendre en compte ; prêter attention à.
target_senses.note: la forme négative « ne pas calculer » est synonyme du mot ignorer

examples.text: « Les élites parisiennes ne nous calculent pas. […] » dénonce Roger de La Rochelle qui « n’a plus honte de ne plus voter ».
Pour maximiser vos chances de tirer le bon numéro, voici les hommes qu’il vaut mieux ne pas calculer !

Les types à qui on parlerait si on se parlait dans ces endroits sont toujours ceux qui traînent leur clope devant la machine à café. On se calcule vite fait, on maintient la distance, indifférence ou pudeur, comme en prison.
